findings.reason: the brief sends the builder to trace two paths its own evidence excludes, so it would either stop blocked or hunt the wrong mechanism while the real question (why `queue_dispatch` left no pointer — e.g. the existing-run answer at `reckon/crew/runs.py:571-580`, or a code revision mismatch) goes unasked.
findings.text: §33's Why concludes the mechanism is untraced, offering "either that compose resolved to a backend other than clive, or the allowance's reason was raised on a path that never reaches the queue branch", but neither survives the evidence: `_dispatch_lane_allowance` builds the grant only from the resolved backend's declared `lane_document` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:1271-1301`, read at `:705`), only `clive` declares one (`~/.config/reckon/flight.yaml:342`), and `clive` is both `local_backend` (`:75`) and `default_backend` (`:45`), so `backend_name == local_backend` at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1461` and the queue branch at `:1546-1552` runs; with no `lineage_override` from `plan_review.dispatch_code_review` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:2780-2790`) the shadow escape is closed too — so the surviving explanation is not "the branch was skipped" but "the branch ran and its write did not persist"

findings.reason: a first case that passes on base measures nothing, so the node could report done with no defect repaired; the plan needs the trace to name the failing case first (a base arm that fails) before the fix is written.
findings.text: §33's first case asserts a queued pointer appears for a composed code review on the local lane with the router granting no worker and the gate not paused, but that is precisely the condition under which `dispatch` already queues today (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1546-1552`: `lane_allowance.get("held")` true and `is_local` true calls `queue_dispatch`), so the case passes on unfixed base; the declared negative control "restores the path the report names" cannot then red it, and the plan records no base-failure demonstration of the 11:49:59 defect
